opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Martin (employee ID E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E033.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Jennifer Martin (E033) is a full-time Analyst. She requested admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, her max is write; admin is only allowed for the role that owns the system (Payroll Specialist). Since the requested level is above her maximum, recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jennifer Martin (E033) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training); admin is never allowed. Requested admin is above max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Jennifer Martin (E033) requested admin access to Payroll. The Security DB identifies her as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors max out at read (write requires advanced training) and admin is never allowed. The requested level (admin) is above her maximum, so grant the maximum: read. (Note: the HR note lists her as full-time, which would allow up to write, but the security record reflects contractor status with basic training; under either interpretation admin is not permitted, and the more restrictive verified maximum applies.)

2. contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full-time Analyst: max write → grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max read → grant read.
